items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Can I believe Alfred Williams, doesn't that, a duplex? The one that boy from England here last year bought one from Alfred Williams.

ctx.x: Well, he did, but he had on the last, he was using a duplex out on the street. It was a duplex snare drum. I think Lester San Diego had one of the models of the one that he had. I think Lester has it now.
Can I believe Alfred Williams, doesn't that, a duplex? The one that boy from England here last year bought one from Alfred Williams. Yeah, I'm not sure. I think it was. I believe it is a duplex.

Because at the time it was only two in town. It was one that was of nickel and one of brass. And my father had both of them. The first one he had bought was the one with brass. And then he gave or traded that one over to a drummer during that period by the name of Wooligan. Now, I think his name was William Wooligan or Bill Wooligan. And he had the nickel one. And that was the only two that I've ever seen. And I do believe the one that San Diego had now is the one that my father had. Is he really? I believe…
